definition: The speed of an aircraft relative to the surrounding air.
The acute angle between the chord line of an airfoil and the relative wind.
The airspeed that provides the greatest distance traveled for a given loss of altitude in still air.
Pressure altitude corrected for nonstandard temperature and, in some definitions, humidity.
The rotation of the aircraft about its lateral axis, raising or lowering the nose.
The rotation of the aircraft about its vertical axis, causing the nose to swing left or right.
The rotation of the aircraft about its longitudinal axis, banking the wings left or right.
A condition in which an airfoil exceeds its critical angle of attack and loses lift abruptly.
The use of control inputs or trim systems to relieve control pressures and maintain a desired attitude.
Wind blowing across the runway or flight path, creating drift and challenge during takeoff, landing, or navigation.
A sudden change in wind speed or direction over a short distance, often associated with turbulence and performance hazards.
The process of flying a desired path or course while compensating for drift and wind.
The process of evaluating information, risk, and alternatives before choosing a course of action.
A racetrack-shaped flight path used to delay aircraft at a specified fix while awaiting clearance or sequencing.
The lowest altitude that allows an aircraft to remain clear of obstacles and terrain under the applicable rules.
